mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly gives the trajectory equation of a projectile launched with initial speed u at an angle θ above the horizontal (taking upward as positive and neglecting air resistance)?

options.A: y = x tanθ + (g x^2)/(2 u^2 cos^2θ)
options.B: y = x tanθ - (g x^2)/(2 u^2 cos^2θ)
options.C: y = x cotθ - (g x^2)/(2 u^2 sin^2θ)
options.D: y = x tanθ - (g x^2)/(2 u^2 sin^2θ)

mcqs.answer: y = x tanθ - (g x^2)/(2 u^2 cos^2θ)
mcqs.explanation: Starting from the horizontal motion x = u cosθ·t and vertical motion y = u sinθ·t - (1/2) g t^2, eliminate t = x/(u cosθ). Substituting gives y = x tanθ - (g x^2)/(2 u^2 cos^2θ). Option B matches this derived expression; the other options have incorrect signs or use cotangent/sine where cosine should appear.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with a speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², what is the total time the projectile remains in the air?
mcqs.explanation: Time of flight T = (2 u sinθ)/g. Here u = 20 m/s, sin30° = 0.5, g = 10 m/s². So T = (2 × 20 × 0.5)/10 = 20/10 = 2 s. Option B is correct; the other values arise from mis‑using the formula or forgetting the factor of 2.

mcqs.question: Which expression gives the maximum height H reached by a projectile launched with initial speed u at an angle θ (upward) from level ground?
mcqs.explanation: Maximum height is obtained from the vertical motion where final vertical velocity is zero: 0 = u sinθ - g t_up, giving t_up = (u sinθ)/g. Substituting into H = u sinθ·t_up - (1/2) g t_up² yields H = (u² sin²θ)/(2g). Option A matches; the others misuse cosine or omit the square of sinθ.

mcqs.question: The horizontal range R of a projectile launched from level ground with speed u at angle θ (neglecting air resistance) is given by:

options.D: Both A and C are correct

mcqs.answer: Both A and C are correct
mcqs.explanation: Using R = (u cosθ)·T and T = (2u sinθ)/g, we get R = (u² sin2θ)/g because sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ. Hence both forms A (explicit sin2θ) and C (expanded) represent the same range. Option D correctly states that both are valid; B is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the projectile’s velocity at launch, at the highest point, and just before landing (assuming launch and landing heights are the same)?

options.A: At launch the velocity is purely horizontal; at the highest point it is purely vertical; just before landing it is again purely horizontal.
options.B: At launch the velocity has both horizontal and vertical components; at the highest point the vertical component is zero while the horizontal component remains unchanged; just before landing the vertical component is downward with the same magnitude as at launch.
options.C: At launch the velocity is zero; at the highest point it is maximum; just before landing it is zero again.
options.D: The magnitude of velocity is constant throughout the motion, only its direction changes.

mcqs.answer: At launch the velocity has both horizontal and vertical components; at the highest point the vertical component is zero while the horizontal component remains unchanged; just before landing the vertical component is downward with the same magnitude as at launch.
mcqs.explanation: Projectile motion combines constant horizontal velocity (u cosθ) with uniformly accelerated vertical motion. At launch both components exist. At the peak, vertical velocity becomes zero, but horizontal component stays u cosθ. Just before landing, vertical velocity equals -u sinθ (same magnitude, opposite direction). Option B captures these facts; the other options misstate the nature of the components.

mcqs.question: A stone is projected from ground level with a speed of 10 m/s at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², what is the horizontal range of the stone?
mcqs.explanation: Range R = (u² sin2θ)/g. Here u = 10 m/s, θ = 45°, so sin2θ = sin90° = 1. Thus R = (10² × 1)/10 = 100/10 = 10 m. Option B is correct; the other values arise from arithmetic errors or using the wrong angle.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with a speed of 25 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. What is the magnitude of the horizontal component of the initial velocity?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component u_x = u cosθ = 25 × cos30°. cos30° = √3/2 ≈ 0.866. Hence u_x ≈ 25 × 0.866 = 21.65 ≈ 21.7 m/s. Option A matches; B uses a slightly larger value, C ignores the cosine factor, D gives the total speed.

mcqs.question: A ball is thrown from a point O with speed u at an angle θ to the horizontal. A friend watches the motion from a point P located directly 5 m horizontally from O. Which of the following equations correctly relates the vertical displacement y of the ball from O to its horizontal displacement x (measured from O) for this scenario?

options.A: y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.B: y = x tanθ + (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.C: y = x cotθ - (g x²)/(2 u² sin²θ)

mcqs.answer: y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
mcqs.explanation: The standard derivation does not depend on the observer’s position; it uses the projectile’s own coordinates. Eliminating time t from x = u cosθ·t and y = u sinθ·t - (1/2) g t² gives y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ). Option A is the correct trajectory equation. Option B has the wrong sign, C uses cotθ incorrectly, and D incorrectly shifts the horizontal coordinate by 5 m.
